fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow fire apparatus and emergency vehicles to reach the residence.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure so responders can move around it freely.
• Mark or post the address visibly on the detached structure if it is not already labeled.
• Clear a direct walking path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings quickly.
• Keep the rear patio area clear of furniture and stored items so responders can move through without obstruction.
• If a rear gate exists, keep it unlocked and confirm it is wide enough for responders carrying equipment.
• Thin dense vegetation at the rear of the property to give responders a clear line of sight and a path to move around the back of the home.
• Identify and mark the location of exterior utility shutoffs so responders can locate them without searching.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster to create gaps between individual trees, reducing the chance that fire moves from tree to tree toward the house.
• Trim lower branches on large trees near the structure to raise the canopy and reduce the path fire can take from the ground up into the trees.
• Remove or cut back shrubs and ground vegetation that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Clear dead grass, leaves, and low ground vegetation from the area immediately surrounding the structure.
• Thin scattered trees that sit between the tree cluster and the structure to break up the connection between them.
• Trim branches and cut back shrubs along both sides of the driveway so the full width stays open and passable for emergency vehicles.
• Keep overhanging branches trimmed above the driveway to allow full clearance for fire trucks and other emergency vehicles.
• Since there is only one way in and out, keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles, debris, and overgrown vegetation at all times so it remains passable during an emergency.
• Mow or cut ground vegetation in open areas between the tree cluster and the structure to reduce the amount of material that could carry fire across that space.
